BASIC floating-point workspace: the tail of FAC2's mantissa ($6B-$6D), its sign ($6E), the
FAC1/FAC2 sign comparison ($6F), FAC1's rounding byte ($70), and FBUFPT ($71-$72), a series
evaluation pointer still holding $A30A inside BASIC ROM. Inherited state; the game's own
zero-page allocation ends at $6A (SAVED_PARSE_INDEX).

CHRGET ($0073-$008A) - executable code living in zero page, not data.
The KERNAL copies this 24-byte routine into RAM at power-up; it is BASIC's tokenizer feed. It
increments the 16-bit text pointer at $7A/$7B, fetches the next program byte through an
absolute LDA whose operand IS $7A/$7B (self-modifying by design), skips spaces, and returns
with carry clear when the byte is an ASCII digit.
Byte-verified against the stock routine:
E6 7A D0 02 E6 7B AD 06 02 C9 3A B0 0A C9 20 F0 EF 38 E9 30 38 E9 D0 60
Unmodified and unreachable here: BASIC ROM is banked out ($01 = $36). TXTPTR reads $0206,
pointing into the BASIC input buffer - residue of the RUN that started the game.

RNDX ($8B-$8F) - BASIC's RND seed, still the stock power-up value 80 4F C7 52 58. The game
never uses BASIC's generator.

KERNAL I/O status and scratch ($90-$B1): STATUS ($90) = $40, the EOI left by the last LOAD;
STKEY ($91) = $FF, no STOP; LDTND ($98) = 0, no logical file open; DFLTN/DFLTO ($99/$9A) = 0
and 3, the default keyboard input and screen output devices; TIME ($A0-$A2), the software
jiffy clock, frozen at $0015AF because the game's IRQ handler never chains to $EA31 and so
never calls UDTIM; and tape/RS-232 temporaries the game never uses. SAL ($AC-$AD) and EAL
($AE-$AF) are the start and end addresses of the last KERNAL LOAD.

KERNAL current-file parameter block ($B2-$C5), the part of zero page the game does write.
$B2-$B3  TAPE1   start of the cassette buffer. RESTORE_SYSTEM_TO_BASIC writes $033C here
($A8A8/$A8AC), reproducing what the KERNAL's RAMTAS does at $FD5F
$B7      FNLEN   filename length
$B9      SA      secondary address. LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART writes 0 at $971D, which tells LOAD
to place the file at the address in MEMUSS rather than honouring the load
address stored in the file's first two bytes
$BA      FA      device number. $9723 writes 8, the first disk drive
$BB-$BC  FNADR   filename pointer, normally set through SETNAM ($FFBD)
$C2      STAL+1  I/O start address high; $A8AE writes $03
$C3-$C4  MEMUSS  the load address LOAD uses when SA = 0; $971F writes the low byte
$C5      LSTX    matrix code of the last key SCNKEY saw; $40 = none
Comparing this block against ZERO_PAGE_BACKUP dates the backup exactly: $A0B7 = 5 and
$A0BB/$A0BC = $9735 are the SETNAM("PART2") parameters written at $9725-$972B, so the backup
half is zero page as LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART left it.
KERNAL NDX: number of characters waiting in the keyboard buffer.

KERNAL screen-editor, keyboard and RS-232 workspace ($C7-$FD). The game reads or writes none of it except $FD; the values are stale state from before the program took the machine over, and they are internally consistent for a stock 40x25 screen at $0400. The game own screen is SCREEN_RAM at $CC00.
$CB SFDX is the matrix code of the key being scanned; $40 means none. $CC BLNSW disables cursor blink. $D1-$D2 point to screen line $0400. $D5 LNMX is $27 (39). $D6 TBLX is the cursor physical line and is not game state. $D9-$F2 is the 26-byte screen line-link table. $F3-$F4 point to Color RAM $D800; $F5-$F6 point to the KERNAL unshifted keyboard table $EB81; $F7-$FA are null RS-232 buffer pointers. $FD is cleared by LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART at $971B with the KERNAL file parameters; its consumer is the fast-loader image under I/O at $DC00-$DFFF, outside this snapshot.
Ghidra 6502 SLEIGH models JSR, RTS, PHA and PLA stack accesses at $00Fx rather than $01Fx, producing roughly 189 false references into $F0-$F9. The only real game access here is $971B writing $FD. The modeled stack traffic nevertheless establishes that the live stack did not descend below $01F0, explaining why the excluded prior-stage bytes at $0100-$01E8 survive unchanged in this later gameplay snapshot.

KERNAL LDTB1 ($D9-$F2) — the screen editor's 26-byte line-link table: one entry per screen row
plus an editor scratch byte. Bits 0-3 hold the screen-memory page displacement of that row's
first byte; bit 7 set marks the first physical line of a logical line. The captured $84/$85/$86/
$87 pattern describes a stock 40x25 screen based at $0400, i.e. state left over from before the
game took the machine. The game neither reads nor writes it; the incoming references are the
6502 stack-modelling artifact described in the KERNAL_EDITOR_WORKSPACE plate at $C7.
Zero-page pointer supplied to KERNAL SAVE as the start of serialized state.
Excluded prior-stage stack-page residue retained as data exactly as captured in the gameplay snapshot. No prior loader, depacker, intro, or crack code is modeled or reversed here.

Live 6510 stack at capture: twelve bytes holding the six nested JSR return addresses of the
documented call chain. No frame of that chain lies below $01F4, which is why $0100-$01E8 is
prior-stage residue rather than active state. JSR stores the address of its final byte, so each
return target is the stored value plus one.
Innermost first: $01F4=$0554 (JSR $FF9F at $0552, KERNAL SCNKEY); $01F6=$055F (JSR $0552 at
$055D, wait for SPACE); $01F8=$1184 (JSR $055D at $1182); $01FA=$169B (self-modified JSR $117A
at $1699); $01FC=$1578 (JSR $1605 at $1576, bytecode interpreter); $01FE=$0408 (JSR $14D6 at
$0406, INIT_GAME).
The VSF CPU PC is $EA93 inside KERNAL SCNKEY, reached through $FF9F, matching the innermost
frame. The machine was blocked at the room-setup SPACE prompt.
Page 1 immediately below $01F4 is not stable: two dumps taken from the same blocked session
differ at $01EC/$01ED, so transient KERNAL and
interrupt frames do reach at least $01EC while the engine waits. Only $01F4-$01FF is asserted.

BASIC_INPUT_BUFFER (BUF, $0200-$0258, 89 bytes), unused by the game. At capture it retains startup residue: $8A is the tokenized RUN keyword and the trailing 8,1 is from an earlier LOAD command. This establishes prior-stage provenance only; the excluded startup code is not modeled in the Ghidra program.

KERNAL_LAT ($0259-$0262) - KERNAL table of active logical file numbers, one byte per open
file, up to ten. All zero here: no logical file is open at capture. Maintained by OPEN/CLOSE,
not by this program.
KERNAL_FAT ($0263-$026C) - KERNAL table of device numbers, parallel to KERNAL_LAT.
KERNAL_SAT ($026D-$0276) - KERNAL table of secondary addresses, parallel to KERNAL_LAT.

KEYBOARD_BUFFER (KEYD, $0277-$0280) - the KERNAL's ten-byte keystroke FIFO.
SCNKEY ($FF9F) scans the keyboard matrix through CIA 1 and appends PETSCII codes here,
bumping the count in NDX ($00C6); GETIN ($FFE4) removes the oldest code and decrements NDX.
The fill limit is XMAX ($0289), default 10.
This program never touches the buffer directly, but it is squarely on the input path: $0552
and $084B call SCNKEY, $0555 and $084E call GETIN, and $083A zeroes NDX to flush pending
keystrokes before reading a command line. Empty at capture.
KERNAL current character color.
KERNAL GDCOL: color value saved from the screen cell under the software cursor so it can be restored when the cursor moves.
KERNAL HIBASE: high byte of the current screen-memory base. $04 selects the standard screen at $0400.
KERNAL XMAX: maximum number of characters accepted in the keyboard buffer. The captured default $0A permits ten queued characters.
KERNAL RPTFLG: keyboard auto-repeat mode. Zero selects the normal policy (cursor keys repeat; other keys do not).
KERNAL key-repeat control flag, cleared after accepted input.

KERNAL_EDITOR_RS232_WORKSPACE ($0291-$02A5) - charset-switch enable, scroll enable, the
mock-6551 RS-232 registers and buffer indices, and cassette save temporaries. All zero: this
program uses none of them.
$02A7-$02FF - documented as unused by the KERNAL, and zero here.

BASIC_VECTORS ($0300-$030B) - IERROR, IMAIN, ICRNCH, IQPLOP, IGONE, IEVAL: ROM BASIC's
indirect entry points.
Still at power-up values ($E38B, $A483, $A57C, $A71A, $A7E4, $AE86) and inert. BASIC ROM is
banked out ($01 = $36), and the RAM those addresses select now holds the game's IRQ handlers
and the object-icon table. Boot residue, not program state.
KERNAL CINV RAM vector. The captured little-endian value $A7E0 installs the game's raster dispatcher; the ROM IRQ entry consults this vector while KERNAL remains mapped in.

KERNAL_IO_VECTORS ($031A-$0333) - indirect entry points for OPEN, CLOSE, CHKIN, CKOUT,
CLRCHN, CHRIN, CHROUT, STOP, GETIN, CLALL, the user command, LOAD and SAVE.
Every one is at its ROM default for KERNAL revision 901227-03 ($F34A, $F291, $F20E, $F250,
$F333, $F157, $F1CA, $F6ED, $F13E, $F32F, $FE66, $F4A5, $F5ED), matching the ROM's own
default table at $FD30. The program never patches them: for disk I/O it calls the public jump
table (SETNAM $FFBD and friends) and lets the KERNAL run normally.
Note Mapping the 64 lists ILOAD/ISAVE as $F49E/$F5DD; this machine runs 901227-03, whose
defaults are $F4A5/$F5ED, and those are the values present.

CASSETTE_BUFFER (TBUFFER, $033C-$03FB) - the KERNAL's 192-byte datasette block buffer.
Unused by a disk-only program, which is exactly why the game parks its resident loader
trampoline RUN_FASTLOADER at $03A0, inside this buffer: 192 bytes that neither BASIC nor the
KERNAL will disturb as long as no tape operation occurs. $033C-$039F is still zero-filled;
the game's code begins at $03A0.

RUN_FASTLOADER ($03A0)
Purpose: Bring the parked custom disk fast-loader into executable space and run it. The image normally lives in the RAM hidden beneath the CIA/I-O window at $DC00-$DFFF; this wrapper exchanges it with the four screen-matrix pages at $CC00-$CFFF and then calls it at $CC00.
Inputs: None in registers. Requires the loader image parked in RAM under $DC00-$DFFF and KERNAL file parameters already set by the caller (LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART performs SETNAM before calling).
Outputs: The requested part has been loaded by the custom loader; the loader image and the previous screen-matrix contents have been exchanged back by the callee's second half, so $CC00-$CFFF again holds the loader image only for the duration of the call.
Assumptions: Entry with $01=$37 so that KERNAL ROM and the I/O page are visible; the four exchange pages exist both at $CC00-$CFFF and in RAM under $DC00-$DFFF.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, plus whatever the custom loader itself uses; the visible screen matrix is destroyed for the duration of the call.
Hardware changes: Indirect: the callee SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE drives the 6510 port $01 between $37 and $38, and the loader itself drives the serial bus on CIA 2 port A ($DD00). The text screen is unreadable while the loader occupies $CC00-$CFFF, which is why the caller blanks the VIC display first.
records.s: Swap the hidden loader into execution space.
Execute the custom loader now resident at $CC00.

records.c:
SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE ($03A6)
Purpose: Exchange the four 256-byte pages at $CC00-$CFFF with the four pages of RAM that lie underneath the I/O window at $DC00-$DFFF, so that a program parked in hidden RAM becomes executable and the displaced screen matrix is preserved.
Inputs: None in registers. Requires four consecutive pages at $CC00 and four underneath $DC00.
Outputs: The two four-page regions have swapped contents. All four self-modified absolute operand high bytes ($03AD, $03B0, $03B3, $03B7) are reset to $CC/$DC so the routine is re-entrant across calls. Returns with interrupts disabled.
Assumptions: Entry with $01=$37. The routine reaches $38 by INC $01, which is only correct from $37; it restores by DEC $01. Interrupts must stay off while I/O is hidden, otherwise an IRQ acknowledging $D019 would write RAM instead.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the four operand bytes named above, and the interrupt-disable flag (left set on return).
Hardware changes: Executes SEI. Changes the 6510 on-chip port $01 from $37 to $38, which unmaps the whole I/O page (VIC-II, SID, CIAs, colour RAM) and exposes the RAM beneath it, then restores $37. No device register is written.

records.s: Increment $01 from $37 to $38: expose RAM at $D000-$DFFF.
Read one byte from the visible $CCxx page; operand high byte advances per page.; Source aliases: SWAP_SRC_VISIBLE_PAGE
Read the corresponding byte from RAM hidden beneath I/O.
Move hidden-RAM byte into the $CCxx loader page.
Store former $CCxx byte under I/O, completing the swap.
Advance the $CCxx read operand to the next page.
Advance the $DCxx read operand to the next page.
Advance the $CCxx write operand to the next page.
Advance the $DCxx write operand to the next page.
Restore $01 from $38 to $37 so ROM and I/O are visible again.
Reset all self-modified operand high bytes for the next invocation.

records.c:
31 zero bytes. $03E1-$03FB is the tail of the KERNAL's cassette buffer ($033C-$03FB) and
$03FC-$03FF is documented as unused; RUN_FASTLOADER / SWAP_FASTLOADER_IMAGE ends with RTS at
$03E0 and nothing follows it.
The game parks its fast-loader wrapper at $03A0-$03E0 for the usual C64 reason: on a
disk-only program the tape buffer is free RAM, and it stays visible in every $01 banking
configuration, including the all-RAM map the swap routine selects. The zeros here are the
KERNAL RAMTAS boot fill.

ENTRY_POINT ($0400)
Purpose: Resident handoff from the excluded startup/intro occupant into gameplay. The two calls at $0400 and $0403 enter excluded byte ranges; the retained boundary fact is that the chain returns at $0406 with the gameplay display, raster IRQ and banking installed. $0406 then initialises the adventure and falls through into the command loop.
Inputs: None in registers. Requires the expanded gameplay image resident in RAM as captured.
Outputs: Gameplay display, IRQ vector and banking installed; adventure state initialised by INIT_GAME; control enters MAIN_LOOP and never returns.
Assumptions: The captured 64 KiB image and an otherwise normal C64. The excluded callees at $069B and $1580 are provenance only; the only asserted contract is that they return with the gameplay display installed.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and effectively the whole engine zero page and state block through callees.
Hardware changes: Through the excluded chain and ENTER_GAMEPLAY_DISPLAY: the 6510 port $01, VIC-II display and interrupt registers, SID, colour RAM, and the KERNAL RAM IRQ vector CINV at $0314/$0315.

records.s: excluded intro; returns with gameplay display installed

records.c:
CALL_INIT_GAME ($0406)
Purpose: Alternate, non-returning entry into game initialisation. Reached by the restart path (JMP from RESTART_GAME at $0FEE). Calls INIT_GAME to rebuild adventure state and the starting room, then falls through into MAIN_LOOP.
Inputs: None in registers.
Outputs: Adventure state rebuilt and the starting room described; control continues in MAIN_LOOP. Never returns to its caller.
Assumptions: The gameplay memory layout, banking, raster IRQ and display are already established; only the adventure state is rebuilt.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and all game state through callees. Any stack frame belonging to the abandoned command is not unwound here; RESTART_GAME has already discarded it.
Hardware changes: None directly. Callees write screen and colour RAM through the terminal.

MAIN_LOOP ($0409)
Purpose: The non-returning foreground command loop: describe the current room, read one edited command line, parse and execute it, repeat forever.
Inputs: None in registers. Requires valid captured PART1 tables and initialised game state.
Outputs: Continuously updated screen and game-state arrays. Never returns; the only exits are the non-local ones taken by RESTART_GAME and ACTION_NEXT_PART.
Assumptions: Runs under the already-established gameplay banking ($01=$36), the raster-split IRQ, and the split display; it does not configure them itself.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the whole parser, VM and renderer workspace.
Hardware changes: None directly; callees write screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF, colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF, and read the CIA 1 keyboard matrix through KERNAL SCNKEY/GETIN.

records.s: read a line of player input

records.c:
SWITCH_TO_NEXT_PART ($0415)
Purpose: Advance the multipart overlay selector and bring in the next story part. Increments CURRENT_PART_NO, sets CURRENT_ROOM to that part's starting room ($34 for part 2, $4D for any later part), shows the swap prompt and loads, runs the new part's initialisation, and resumes the command loop.
Inputs: CURRENT_PART_NO ($2940) valid; the replacement disk part available in the drive.
Outputs: CURRENT_PART_NO incremented, CURRENT_ROOM set, the captured overlay replaced on disk load, LOADED_PART_NO ($5E) recorded, and control transferred to MAIN_LOOP. Non-returning with respect to the action handler that invoked it.
Assumptions: Called only from ACTION_NEXT_PART, which has already discarded three levels of return address, so the stack is at the main-loop level. The replacement occupant's internals are outside this project.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, UI and disk scratch, and every array the replacement occupant's initialisation script writes.
Hardware changes: Through its callees: VIC-II display enable and border/background, VIC interrupt enable $D01A, CIA 1 timer A control $DC0E and interrupt control $DC0D, the serial bus, and the 6510 port $01.

records.s: show 'part N' screen + load from disk

records.c: Pointer to ROOM_GRAPHIC_TABLE, the fixed six-byte illustration-blit records.
Pointer to the three-entry per-part initialization-script pointer table.

SHOW_PART_LOAD_SCREEN ($0439)
Purpose: Print the "insert part N" prompt, wait for Space, then load that part through the resident fast loader and record which part is now resident.
Inputs: CURRENT_PART_NO ($2940) selects the prompt digit and the file to load.
Outputs: The prompt and the digit CURRENT_PART_NO+'0' printed; the requested part loaded over the overlay region; LOADED_PART_NO ($5E) set to CURRENT_PART_NO; returns normally.
Assumptions: Terminal, keyboard, the installed loader at $9700 and the drive are all available. Gameplay interrupts are suspended and restored by PREPARE_DISK_IO/END_DISK_IO around the load.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the whole text-renderer scratch, and the zero page (exchanged with its backup and exchanged back).
Hardware changes: Blanks and re-enables the VIC display through $D011 bit 4 (DEN); rewrites the VIC interrupt-enable register $D01A ($F0 then $F1); stops CIA 1 timer A through $DC0E bit 0; drives the serial bus; changes the 6510 port $01 during the load.

LOAD_DISABLED_RTS ($045F)
Purpose: One-byte return stub standing in for the LOAD feature. Action opcode $13 jumps here instead of to the surviving KERNAL load implementation at DISK_LOAD_GAME, so the shipped LOAD verb does nothing.
Inputs: None. Also called (as a plain subroutine) by DO_RESTART at $14F3.
Outputs: Immediate return with everything unchanged.
Assumptions: Nothing; the stub is deliberately inert. The complete load implementation still exists at $0461 but no shipped rule reaches it.
Clobbers: Nothing. A, X, Y, flags, memory, banking and devices are all preserved.
Hardware changes: None.

Single shipped $00 separator between the one-byte NOOP_045F RTS stub and DISK_LOAD_GAME. The byte is present in the original NEVER ENDING disk file, has no decoded operand or recorded reference, and is not on any control-flow path.

DISK_LOAD_GAME ($0461)
Purpose: Complete but unreachable KERNAL restore-game implementation: prompt for a filename, LOAD the saved state block over OBJECT_LOCATIONS, pull in a different story part if the restored save belongs to one, then redescribe and repaint the room.
Inputs: A = mode flag stored into DISK_ERROR_FLAG ($5F). DISK_LOAD_ADDR ($28BB/$28BC) supplies the load address; the eight-character FILENAME_BUF ($0DD7) is filled by READ_FILENAME.
Outputs: On success the saved state block is in memory, the room is redescribed and the picture repainted. On a carry-set KERNAL error it tail-jumps to DISK_IO_ERROR. Returns normally otherwise.
Assumptions: Static audit finds no call, pointer, action script or decoded operand reaching $0461 in the shipped build, so this routine is retained but inactive; the SAVE/LOAD verbs dispatch to the no-op stubs instead. When it did run it required KERNAL ROM, I/O and the KERNAL zero page to be swapped in by PREPARE_DISK_IO.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, DISK_ERROR_FLAG, the zero page (exchanged and restored), and the whole renderer workspace.
Hardware changes: Through its callees: 6510 port $01 during the zero-page exchange, VIC-II display enable $D011 bit 4, VIC interrupt enable $D01A, CIA 1 timer A control $DC0E, and the serial bus via KERNAL LOAD ($FFD5), SETLFS ($FFBA) and SETNAM ($FFBD). Executes SEI around the status check.

SAVE_DISABLED_RTS ($0491)
Purpose: One-byte return stub standing in for the SAVE feature. Action opcode $12 jumps here instead of to the surviving KERNAL save implementation at DISK_SAVE_GAME.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: Immediate return with everything unchanged.
Assumptions: Nothing; the stub is deliberately inert. The orphaned pointer word $04C8 stored at $0492/$0493 is leftover metadata of the disabled subsystem, not a live vector.
Clobbers: Nothing. A, X, Y, flags, memory, banking and devices are all preserved.
Hardware changes: None.

UNUSED_READ_FILENAME_PTR — orphaned little-endian pointer $04C8 to READ_FILENAME, retained beside the disabled save/load implementation.
The shipped vocabulary accepts SAVE and LOAD, but their action scripts are only `12 FF` and `13 FF`; those opcode handlers jump to NOOP_0491 and NOOP_045F. No pointer, call, action script, decoded operand, or recorded reference reaches DISK_LOAD_GAME, DISK_SAVE_GAME, or this word. The bytes are unchanged from the original NEVER ENDING PRG. Their exact value and placement immediately after the save verb's RTS identify leftover filename-routine metadata from the disabled feature, not active code or an unresolved target.

DISK_SAVE_GAME ($0494)
Purpose: Complete but unreachable KERNAL save-game implementation: copy the save start address into the KERNAL's zero-page pointer at $FE/$FF, set the file parameters, and SAVE from there up to DISK_SAVE_END_ADDR.
Inputs: DISK_LOAD_ADDR ($28BB/$28BC) is the start of the block to write; DISK_SAVE_END_ADDR ($28BD/$28BE) is the exclusive end; FILENAME_BUF holds the eight-character name.
Outputs: On success the block is written and END_DISK_IO restores the gameplay machine state. On a carry-set KERNAL error it tail-jumps to DISK_IO_ERROR.
Assumptions: Static audit finds no active caller; the SAVE verb dispatches to SAVE_DISABLED_RTS. KERNAL SAVE requires A to hold the zero-page address of the start pointer, hence the LDA #$FE.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the KERNAL save pointer at $FE/$FF, and the zero page (exchanged and restored).
Hardware changes: 6510 port $01 during the zero-page exchange; VIC-II display enable $D011 bit 4; VIC interrupt enable $D01A; CIA 1 timer A control $DC0E; the serial bus via KERNAL SAVE ($FFD8), SETLFS and SETNAM. Executes SEI around the status check.

records.s: A=$FE => ZP ptr holding start address

records.c:
DISK_IO_ERROR ($04B6)
Purpose: Shared failure tail for the retained disk subsystem: restore the gameplay machine state, raise the error flag, and print the disk-error message.
Inputs: Entered by tail jump from DISK_LOAD_GAME ($0478) or DISK_SAVE_GAME ($04B0) with carry set from the KERNAL call, or from ABORT_EMPTY_FILENAME at the $04B9 continuation.
Outputs: DISK_ERROR_FLAG ($5F) set to 1; sentence $12 printed; returns to the caller of the failed disk routine.
Assumptions: END_DISK_IO must be able to swap the game zero page back in, so the backup at $A002-$A0FF must be intact and BASIC must be banked out.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, DISK_ERROR_FLAG, zero page (exchanged), and text-renderer scratch.
Hardware changes: Through END_DISK_IO: re-enables the VIC display ($D011 bit 4), stops CIA 1 timer A ($DC0E bit 0), rewrites $D01A to $F1 and executes CLI. Writes screen and colour RAM through the terminal.

ABORT_EMPTY_FILENAME ($04C3)
Purpose: Abort the filename prompt when the player entered nothing. Discards the immediate caller's return address so control cannot fall back into the load/save flow, then joins the error tail at $04B9.
Inputs: Entered by branch from READ_FILENAME ($04D5) with INPUT_LEN ($26) zero.
Outputs: Two bytes popped from the stack; DISK_ERROR_FLAG set to 1 and sentence $12 printed; the eventual RTS returns to the caller of the routine that called READ_FILENAME.
Assumptions: The stack contains exactly READ_FILENAME's return address on top, i.e. this label is only reachable from inside READ_FILENAME.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, DISK_ERROR_FLAG, six bytes of stack depth accounting (two popped here), and renderer scratch.
Hardware changes: Writes screen and colour RAM through the terminal; no device register is programmed here.

READ_FILENAME ($04C8)
Purpose: Prompt for and normalise an eight-character disk filename: print the prompt sentence, read one line with the long idle timeout, blank the buffer, then copy up to eight characters while folding lowercase to uppercase.
Inputs: None in registers. Uses the edited line left by READ_INPUT_ALT at INPUT_TEXT_BUFFER ($CBA0) with its length in INPUT_LEN ($26) and its pointer in AUX_PTR ($0E/$0F).
Outputs: FILENAME_BUF ($0DD7-$0DDE) contains eight characters, space padded, PETSCII uppercase. Empty input does not return; it diverts to ABORT_EMPTY_FILENAME.
Assumptions: Case folding is a plain SBC #$20 applied to every non-space character, so it only produces correct results for lowercase letters; digits and punctuation are mangled. Retained inactive code.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags, FILENAME_BUF, and everything READ_INPUT_ALT clobbers (editor state, idle counters, cursor).
Hardware changes: Through the editor: reads the CIA 1 keyboard matrix via KERNAL SCNKEY ($FF9F) and GETIN ($FFE4); writes screen and colour RAM.

BLANK_FILENAME_BUF ($04EB)
Purpose: Fill the eight-byte FILENAME_BUF with PETSCII spaces so a short name is correctly padded for KERNAL SETNAM.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: FILENAME_BUF ($0DD7-$0DDE) set to $20 eight times. Returns with X=$FF and N set.
Assumptions: The buffer is exactly eight bytes and is followed by the orphaned metadata word, which this loop does not touch.
Clobbers: A, X, flags. Y is preserved.
Hardware changes: None; ordinary RAM only.

PREPARE_DISK_IO ($04F6)
Purpose: Put the machine into a state in which KERNAL disk routines can run: disable interrupts, exchange the game's private zero page for the KERNAL's, blank the display, and disable the raster interrupt source.
Inputs: None. Requires the KERNAL zero-page image to be present in the backup at $A002-$A0FF.
Outputs: The KERNAL zero page is live and the game's copy is parked in the backup; the display is blank; the VIC raster interrupt is masked; returns with interrupts still disabled.
Assumptions: BASIC ROM must be banked out ($01=$36 or $35) so that reads from $A000-$A0FF see the backup RAM rather than ROM. The four NOPs at $04F7-$04FA are shipped padding.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the entire zero page from $02 to $FF (exchanged with its backup).
Hardware changes: Executes SEI. Clears bit 4 (DEN) of VIC-II control register 1 $D011, blanking the display. Writes $F0 to the VIC interrupt-enable register $D01A, clearing bit 0 so raster compares no longer request an IRQ.

records.s: swap in KERNAL zero page (restore $02-$FF from $A000 backup)

records.c:
SETUP_KERNAL_FILE ($050C)
Purpose: Establish the KERNAL file parameters for the retained save/load code: logical file $20 on device 8 with secondary address 0, and an eight-character name taken from FILENAME_BUF.
Inputs: FILENAME_BUF filled; FILENAME_PTR ($0DD5/$0DD6) points at it.
Outputs: KERNAL SETLFS and SETNAM have recorded the file number, device, secondary address, name length and name pointer.
Assumptions: Secondary address 0 selects a program-file load at the address stored in the file rather than at the caller's address; the retained load path overrides that by passing A=0 to LOAD with its own X/Y.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the KERNAL's own zero-page file-parameter bytes.
Hardware changes: Calls KERNAL SETLFS ($FFBA) and SETNAM ($FFBD); no device is accessed yet.

END_DISK_IO ($0521)
Purpose: Undo PREPARE_DISK_IO: bring the game's zero page back, re-enable the display, stop CIA 1 timer A, re-arm the raster interrupt, and re-enable interrupts.
Inputs: None. Requires the game zero page to be parked in the backup at $A002-$A0FF.
Outputs: Game zero page live again; display enabled; CIA 1 timer A halted; VIC raster interrupt re-armed; interrupts enabled on return.
Assumptions: BASIC must still be banked out so the backup region reads as RAM. The routine assumes the raster dispatcher at $A7E0 is still installed in CINV.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the entire zero page from $02 to $FF.
Hardware changes: Executes SEI then CLI. Sets bit 4 (DEN) of $D011 to re-enable the display. Clears bit 0 of CIA 1 timer A control $DC0E, stopping the timer that would otherwise drive the KERNAL's 60 Hz interrupt. Writes $F1 to $D01A, enabling the raster-compare interrupt source.
records.s: swap game zero page back in

records.c:
SWAP_ZERO_PAGE_AND_BACKUP ($053C)
Purpose: Exchange the 254 bytes of zero page from $02 to $FF with the backup block at $A002-$A0FF, so the same code can serve both directions: park the game workspace before a KERNAL call and restore it afterwards.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: The two regions have exchanged contents. Returns with Y=$01 and X holding the last byte read from zero page.
Assumptions: $00 and $01 are deliberately excluded: they are the 6510 data-direction and port registers, not ordinary RAM, and swapping them would change the memory map mid-loop. BASIC ROM must be banked out so $A000-$A0FF reads the backup RAM; a write-only mapping is not enough because every byte is read before being replaced.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, zero page $02-$FF, and the backup block.
Hardware changes: None directly, but the routine is only correct under a banking configuration that hides BASIC ROM.

WAIT_FOR_KEY ($0552)
Purpose: Block until the keyboard produces a non-zero PETSCII code, scanning the matrix explicitly rather than relying on the KERNAL's timer interrupt.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: A = the pressed key code, guaranteed non-zero; flags reflect the CMP #$00 that fell through.
Assumptions: KERNAL ROM and the I/O page are visible and the KERNAL's keyboard-related zero-page workspace is valid. Because the game normally runs with CIA 1 timer A stopped, the KERNAL's own keyboard scan is not running, which is why SCNKEY is called explicitly.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the KERNAL keyboard buffer and its associated zero-page bytes.
Hardware changes: Calls KERNAL SCNKEY ($FF9F), which drives the CIA 1 keyboard matrix through $DC00/$DC01, and GETIN ($FFE4), which consumes the keyboard queue. No display register is touched.

WAIT_FOR_SPACE_KEY ($055D)
Purpose: Block until the player presses Space, discarding every other key.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: A = $20; flags reflect the CMP #$20 that fell through.
Assumptions: Same KERNAL ROM, I/O and zero-page requirements as WAIT_FOR_KEY.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, KERNAL keyboard workspace.
Hardware changes: Through WAIT_FOR_KEY: CIA 1 keyboard matrix scanning via KERNAL SCNKEY and GETIN.

CHECK_YES_KEY ($0565)
Purpose: Read exactly one key and classify it as confirmation. Carry is the Boolean result.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: A = the key that was pressed; carry set only for uppercase PETSCII 'Y' ($59), clear for everything else.
Assumptions: Same KERNAL ROM, I/O and zero-page requirements as WAIT_FOR_KEY. The comparison is exact: lowercase 'y' does not confirm.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, KERNAL keyboard workspace.
Hardware changes: Through WAIT_FOR_KEY: CIA 1 keyboard matrix scanning via KERNAL SCNKEY and GETIN.

RENDER_ROOM_GRAPHICS ($0570)
Purpose: Rebuild the whole illustration band: restore the packed base display, draw each active runtime object record, then draw the static room picture selected by CURRENT_ROOM_GRAPHIC_ID.
Inputs: CURRENT_ROOM_GRAPHIC_ID ($2942) selects a RoomGraphicRecord in the 57-entry table at $0BF9; VISIBLE_OBJECT_RECORDS ($2943) holds six six-byte runtime records whose byte 3 is the enable flag.
Outputs: Bitmap RAM at $E000, the screen matrix at $CC00 and colour RAM at $D800 hold the composed picture. Returns by falling into BLIT_ROOM_GRAPHIC's tail.
Assumptions: The record index multiplication is performed as six repeated additions of CURRENT_ROOM_GRAPHIC_ID, which is the six-byte record stride; the caller must keep the index inside the table.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, LOOP_COUNTER ($4B), GRAPHIC_RECORD_PTR ($5A/$5B), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), the blit state at $50-$59, and MEMCPY's pointers.
Hardware changes: Writes colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF directly. Writes bitmap and screen memory, which the VIC-II reads from bank 3. No VIC register is programmed here; the raster handler already selected the modes.
records.s: Restore the packed base room display before overlay rendering.
multiply CURRENT_ROOM_GRAPHIC_ID by the six-byte RoomGraphicRecord stride

records.c:
BLIT_ROOM_GRAPHIC ($05BF)
Purpose: Draw one RoomGraphicRecord. Copies the six record fields into the zero-page blit state and then, for each character row, writes the record's bitmap, screen-code and colour spans to the three destination tables.
Inputs: GRAPHIC_RECORD_PTR ($5A/$5B) points at a six-byte record: start row, start column, source pointer (two bytes), height in rows, width in columns.
Outputs: A height-by-width rectangle of the picture band updated in bitmap, screen and colour memory; BLIT_ROW ($50) advanced to the end row.
Assumptions: Row and column stay inside the ten-row, forty-column destination tables at $0BBD (bitmap), $0BD1 (screen) and $0BE5 (colour). No clipping is performed. The source stream is interleaved per row as width*8 bitmap bytes, then width screen bytes, then width colour bytes, so one record consumes height*width*10 bytes.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the blit state $50-$59 (row, column, source pointer, end row, width, destination pointer, source end pointer).
Hardware changes: Writes colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF; writes bitmap and screen memory read by the VIC-II. Programs no VIC register.

COPY_BLIT_ROW ($0676)
Purpose: Copy one span of the interleaved picture stream to its destination, advancing both pointers across page boundaries and stopping on an exact sixteen-bit end comparison.
Inputs: BLIT_SOURCE_PTR ($52/$53), BLIT_SOURCE_END_PTR ($58/$59) as an exclusive end, and BLIT_DEST_PTR ($56/$57).
Outputs: The span is copied; source and destination pointers are left at their ends, so the caller can compute the next span from BLIT_SOURCE_PTR alone.
Assumptions: The end pointer is strictly reachable from the start pointer; the loop tests low byte then high byte, so a mismatched pair would run away. Y is held at zero throughout, so the indirect stores are effectively plain pointer writes.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags, BLIT_SOURCE_PTR and BLIT_DEST_PTR. X is preserved.
Hardware changes: Writes colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF when the destination is a colour span; otherwise writes ordinary RAM that the VIC-II reads.

records.s: Dynamic GET FALKOR proof: this indirect read used BLIT_SOURCE_PTR=$B3C0 with CURRENT_OBJECT_INDEX=$17; slot 23 is ICON_FALKOR.

records.c:
READ_RASTER_LINE ($0695)
Purpose: Sample the low eight bits of the VIC-II raster counter, used by the engine as its only entropy source.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: A = the low eight bits of $D012; N and Z reflect that value. X and Y are preserved.
Assumptions: The I/O page must be visible. Bit 8 of the raster counter lives in bit 7 of $D011 and is deliberately not returned, so the value wraps every 256 lines rather than every frame.
Clobbers: A and flags only.
Hardware changes: Reads VIC-II register $D012. Nothing is written and no VIC state changes.

NOOP_0699 ($0699)
Purpose: Deliberate one-byte RTS stub invoked by action opcode $0B through NOOP_ACTION_11.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: Immediate return.
Assumptions: The engine allocates one no-op opcode and one stub per silent verb; this is the $0B stub, distinct from the $0C stub at $069A.
Clobbers: Nothing. A, X, Y, flags, memory and devices are all preserved.
Hardware changes: None.

NOOP_069A ($069A)
Purpose: Deliberate one-byte RTS stub invoked by action opcode $0C through NOOP_ACTION_12.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: Immediate return.
Assumptions: Paired with NOOP_0699; the two adjacent stubs exist so that each no-op opcode has its own handler chain.
Clobbers: Nothing. A, X, Y, flags, memory and devices are all preserved.
Hardware changes: None.
Excluded pre-game intro setup bytes retained exactly from the gameplay snapshot. This prior-stage code is not reversed.

ENTER_GAMEPLAY_DISPLAY ($070F)
Purpose: The gameplay-side half of the phase transition: set up the text cursor, clear the text screen, install the runtime disk loader over the excluded title-stage occupant, capture the live bitmap into the packed display buffer, restore the composed display, and install the raster-split IRQ handler.
Inputs: None in registers. Requires the staged loader image at $C000-$C1FF and the live picture already present at $E000; the previous phase has already selected VIC bank 3, enabled the raster interrupt in $D01A and programmed an initial $D012/$D011 compare.
Outputs: SCREEN_CURSOR_PTR ($06/$07) = $CD90 and COLOR_CURSOR_PTR ($08/$09) = $D990; the text screen is cleared; the 512-byte loader occupies $9700-$98FF; $BC00 onwards holds the packed $0FA0-byte display bundle; the composed display is restored; CINV ($0314/$0315) = $A7E0; $01 = $36; interrupts enabled on return.
Assumptions: The copy loop at $0730 runs with $01=$36, so $9700 is plain RAM. Reading the live bitmap at $E000 requires $01=$35 to expose RAM under the KERNAL, which the routine sets and then restores.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, MEMCPY_SOURCE ($0A/$0B), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), the screen and colour cursors, CURRENT_COLUMN ($24), KEY_REPEAT_COUNTDOWN ($028B), the renderer state byte at $0AF5, and the two pages at $9700-$98FF.
Hardware changes: Executes SEI then CLI. Writes the 6510 port $01 ($35 then $36). Sets VIC-II background colour $D021 and border colour $D020 to medium grey ($0C). Writes colour RAM at $D800-$D98F (400 cells) through the display restore. Rewrites the KERNAL RAM IRQ vector CINV at $0314/$0315 to point at $A7E0.
records.s: Keep interrupts disabled while replacing display and IRQ state.
Set screen cursor to $CD90, the first gameplay text position.
Clear all four pages of screen RAM.
Select blue as the KERNAL text color.
Set border and background to medium grey ($0C).

records.c: INSTALL_DISK_LOADER — copies the 512-byte runtime disk loader from staging pages $C000-$C1FF to $9700-$98FF. Y counts 0..255 for both pages in parallel. Called only from ENTER_GAMEPLAY_DISPLAY with $01=$36, so the destination is plain RAM. Replacing the excluded title-stage occupant marks the transition into gameplay.
records.s: Copy staged loader page $C000 to runtime page $9700.
Copy staged loader page $C100 to runtime page $9800.
Expose RAM beneath KERNAL before reading the live bitmap.
MEMCPY destination = packed display buffer at $BC00.
Copy an additional $A0 bytes, for $0FA0 bytes total.
Copy the complete $0FA0-byte packed display bundle.
Restore saved screen, color, and bitmap buffers.
Install gameplay raster dispatcher $A7E0 in the KERNAL IRQ vector.

records.c:
MEMCPY ($0779)
Purpose: General forward block copy of X complete pages plus an optional Y-byte tail, used for the display bundle, screen scrolling and buffer restores.
Inputs: MEMCPY_SOURCE ($0A/$0B) = source, WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D) = destination, X = number of whole 256-byte pages, Y = tail length in bytes.
Outputs: The requested bytes are copied. The two pointer low bytes are unchanged; their high bytes have been incremented by the original X. When the tail was non-zero the routine returns with Y equal to the tail length.
Assumptions: The copy is strictly forward and does not handle overlapping ranges where the destination is above the source within the same page. The tail bound is not a register: it is written into the CPY immediate operand at $079E, so the routine is self-modifying and not interrupt-reentrant.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, SCRATCH_BYTE_2 ($04), the high bytes of both pointers, and the immediate operand byte at $079E, which retains the most recent non-zero tail length.
Hardware changes: None of its own; the destination may be colour RAM or VIC-visible RAM depending on the caller.
records.s: Preserve the requested tail length in zero-page scratch $04.
Skip the full-page loop when X is zero.
Advance source pointer by one page.
Advance destination pointer by one page.
Patch the CPY immediate operand with the tail length.

records.c:
RESTORE_GAMEPLAY_DISPLAY ($07A2)
Purpose: Repaint the whole gameplay display from the three packed buffers: 400 screen cells from $C880 to $CC00, 400 colour cells from $CA10 to $D800, and the $0C80-byte picture from $BC00 to $E000.
Inputs: None in registers; the three packed buffers must hold the composed base display.
Outputs: Screen matrix, colour RAM and bitmap memory all restored to the base picture, ready for object overlays to be drawn on top.
Assumptions: Runs with $01=$36. That leaves KERNAL ROM readable at $E000-$FFFF, but the routine only ever writes there, and writes always fall through to the RAM underneath, which is the RAM the VIC-II fetches the bitmap from in bank 3; no $35 switch is needed because nothing here reads $E000. Writing colour RAM requires the I/O page to be visible, which $36 provides.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, MEMCPY_SOURCE ($0A/$0B), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), and MEMCPY's self-modified tail operand.
Hardware changes: Writes colour RAM at $D800-$D98F (400 cells, X=$01/Y=$90). Writes screen and bitmap memory read by the VIC-II. Programs no VIC register.

records.s: Copy one page plus $90 bytes: 400 screen cells.
Copy one page plus $90 bytes: 400 color cells.
Copy twelve pages plus $80 bytes: $0C80 bytes.

records.c:
CLEAR_TEXT_SCREEN ($07E8)
Purpose: Fill all four pages of the gameplay screen matrix at $CC00-$CFFF with the space screen code.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: 1024 bytes of $20 written at $CC00. Colour RAM is not touched.
Assumptions: The screen matrix is at $CC00 in VIC bank 3, which is where $D018=$38/$3E place it. Runs with the I/O page mapped but never writes it.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and MEMCPY_SOURCE ($0A/$0B), which is left pointing one page past the screen.
Hardware changes: None; ordinary RAM that the VIC-II reads.
records.s: Point the clear loop at screen RAM $CC00.

records.c:
READ_INPUT_ALT ($0801)
Purpose: Alternate entry into the line editor used by the retained filename prompt. It sets only the high byte of the three-byte idle countdown to $FF and joins READ_INPUT at $080E, preserving the existing low and middle bytes and therefore giving a much longer idle timeout than READ_INPUT's own $0004FFFF initialisation.
Inputs: The existing IDLE_COUNTDOWN low and middle bytes ($60/$61).
Outputs: As READ_INPUT: a lowercased command line in INPUT_TEXT_BUFFER ($CBA0) with its length in INPUT_LEN ($26).
Assumptions: Same terminal, KERNAL and banking assumptions as READ_INPUT. Only reachable from READ_FILENAME, which is itself retained inactive code.
Clobbers: As READ_INPUT.
Hardware changes: As READ_INPUT: CIA 1 keyboard scanning through KERNAL SCNKEY/GETIN, plus screen and colour RAM writes.

READ_INPUT ($0806)
Purpose: Read and edit one command line with echo, backspace and an idle timeout. Return finishes the line, Delete backspaces, Space and A-Z are appended after folding to lowercase, and everything else is ignored.
Inputs: None in registers. Uses the terminal cursors at $06-$09 and CURRENT_COLUMN ($24).
Outputs: A lowercased command line of up to 78 characters at INPUT_TEXT_BUFFER ($CBA0) with its length in INPUT_LEN ($26); the line has been echoed on screen and terminated with a blank line. On timeout the line is finished automatically and sentence $13 is printed.
Assumptions: KERNAL ROM and the I/O page must be visible and the KERNAL's keyboard workspace usable, because the editor calls SCNKEY and GETIN directly rather than waiting on a timer interrupt. The buffer is 81 bytes and the editor stops appending at 78.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, IDLE_COUNTDOWN ($60-$62), AUX_PTR ($0E/$0F), INPUT_LEN, KEYBOARD_BUFFER_LEN ($C6), CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR ($0286), KEY_REPEAT_COUNTDOWN ($028B), CURRENT_COLUMN, the terminal cursors, and the self-modified caret-gate operand at $0949.
Hardware changes: Reads the CIA 1 keyboard matrix through KERNAL SCNKEY ($FF9F) and GETIN ($FFE4). Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through PRINT_CHARACTER.

FINISH_INPUT_LINE ($08CD)
Purpose: Close a command line: disable the input caret, restore the ordinary blue text colour, and advance to a fresh line.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: The caret gate at $0949 cleared to zero, CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR ($0286) set to 6 (blue), and a blank line emitted so the cursor sits at column zero. Normally returns with A=$00 and Z set.
Assumptions: The caret gate is an immediate operand inside PRINT_CHARACTER's scroll tail, so clearing it here suppresses the caret for all subsequent output until the editor sets it again.
Clobbers: A, flags, the caret-gate operand at $0949, CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR, CURRENT_COLUMN and the terminal cursors.
Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through PRINT_CHARACTER.

PRINT_CHARACTER ($08DB)
Purpose: Write one screen code at the terminal cursor in the current colour, advance both cursors and the column, wrap at column 39, and scroll the text window when the cursor passes the last row. Every character the engine prints goes through here.
Inputs: A = screen code. SCREEN_CURSOR_PTR ($06/$07), COLOR_CURSOR_PTR ($08/$09), CURRENT_COLUMN ($24) and CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR ($0286).
Outputs: One screen cell and its colour cell written; both sixteen-bit cursors incremented; CURRENT_COLUMN advanced or reset to zero; the window scrolled and the caret optionally repainted.
Assumptions: The two cursors must stay in step and inside the text window at $CD90-$CFFF / $D990-$DBFF. The scroll test compares the screen cursor against the literal $CFC0, so it only triggers on exact arrival at the last row.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, both cursors, CURRENT_COLUMN, and, when scrolling, MEMCPY_SOURCE/WORK_PTR and MEMCPY's self-modified tail operand.
Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF. Colour RAM is only four bits wide, so the stored colour reads back as the low nibble.

When the cursor reaches $CFC0 (start of the screen's last text row) the text window is
scrolled up one row: screen rows are block-moved up ($CDB8->$CD90, ~560 bytes) and the
matching color RAM is moved ($D9B8->$D990); the cursor is reset to $CFC0 and the new last
row (40 cells) is cleared to spaces.

records.s: ↑Cursor is past the end of screen RAM?
scroll color RAM up to match
Mirrors the copy above, for color RAM (D9B8h/D800h)
A = caret-enable flag (operand at $0949 is self-modified); 0 -> skip caret, nonzero -> DRAW_INPUT_CURSOR

records.c:
DRAW_INPUT_CURSOR ($094C)
Purpose: Paint the line-input caret, screen code $3D in light grey, at the current terminal position. Reached from PRINT_CHARACTER's scroll tail only when the caret gate is enabled, so the caret follows every echoed keystroke.
Inputs: SCREEN_CURSOR_PTR ($06/$07) and COLOR_CURSOR_PTR ($08/$09). The gate is the immediate operand at $0949, written from outside PRINT_CHARACTER by the editor ($082E and $08B7 enable it, $0891 and FINISH_INPUT_LINE at $08CF clear it).
Outputs: One screen cell set to $3D and its colour cell set to $0F (light grey).
Assumptions: This is not debug code: it is the only caret the engine draws, and it is deliberately suppressed outside line editing so ordinary narrative output leaves no stray character.
Clobbers: A, X, flags. Y is preserved.
Hardware changes: Writes one screen cell in $CC00-$CFFF and one colour cell in $D800-$DBFF.

PRINT_ROOM_TEXT_DROPCAP ($0957)
Purpose: Render the first letter of a room description as a two-by-two drop capital built from four consecutive custom glyphs, in light grey, then restore the previous text colour.
Inputs: A = the top-left glyph code. The caller derives it as $7B + 4*(letter - 'A') from the description's leading letter.
Outputs: Four screen cells and their colour cells written: the top pair, then thirty-eight spaces in the caller's colour to reach the next row, then the bottom pair. CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR ($0286) is restored to its entry value.
Assumptions: The gameplay character set at $F800 contains the four-cell drop-cap glyphs at $7B upwards, and the terminal cursor is at the start of a row so that the thirty-eight-space advance lands the bottom pair directly underneath the top pair.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, SCRATCH_BYTE ($02), SCRATCH_INDEX ($03), SAVED_CHAR_COLOR ($05), the terminal cursors and CURRENT_COLUMN.
Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through PRINT_CHARACTER.

PRINT_SENTENCE ($099B)
Purpose: Print one common sentence, preceded by a blank line and with its first letter capitalised. This is the engine's standard way of emitting a canned reply.
Inputs: A = common-sentence id.
Outputs: A blank line, then the selected compressed term stream rendered with word wrapping. Tail-jumps into COMPUTE_SENTENCE_PTR_OFS, so the caller's RTS is the renderer's.
Assumptions: SENTENCE_POINTERS ($1CB0, reached through the base pointer at $1C69) contains a valid entry for the id; ids are not range checked.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG ($0AFF), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23), WORD_REMAINING_LEN ($25), the terminal cursors and CURRENT_COLUMN.
Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through the renderer.

COMPUTE_SENTENCE_PTR_OFS ($09AA)
Purpose: Resolve a common-sentence id into a term-stream pointer and render it. Doubles the id, adds the sixteen-bit table base, loads the two-byte entry into TERM_DATA_PTR and tail-jumps to PROCESS_TERM.
Inputs: A = common-sentence id. The sentence pointer table base is the word at $1C69.
Outputs: TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23) points at the sentence's term stream, which is then rendered. Control leaves through PROCESS_TERM, so this routine never returns on its own.
Assumptions: The doubling is done with ASL and a carry test, which supports ids up to 255 and therefore table offsets up to 510. It does not check the id against the table length.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags, WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), TERM_DATA_PTR, and everything the renderer clobbers.
Hardware changes: Writes screen and colour RAM through the renderer; no device register is programmed.
Compute sentence pointer

PRINT_EVENT_TEXT ($09D7)
Purpose: Render one event-text entry: capitalise the first letter, emit a blank line and a two-space paragraph indent, then resolve the id through the event pointer table and render the stream.
Inputs: A = event-text id. The event pointer table base is the word at $2F02.
Outputs: A new indented paragraph containing the event text. Tail-jumps to PROCESS_TERM.
Assumptions: Event ids are supplied by captured PART1 bytecode and are not range checked. Because the base pointer lives in the replaceable overlay, the same id means different text after a part change.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG ($0AFF), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23), and the terminal state.
Hardware changes: Writes screen and colour RAM through the renderer.

records.s: Print a blank line and two-space paragraph indent before the event text.

records.c:
PROCESS_TERM ($0A0E)
Purpose: Interpret one compressed term stream with word wrapping until the '@' terminator. Bytes with bit 7 set are dictionary tokens and are expanded; other bytes begin a literal word whose length is measured before printing so that a word which would cross column 40 is preceded by a line break.
Inputs: TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23) points at the stream; CURRENT_COLUMN ($24) is the live column; UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG ($0AFF) selects capitalisation of the next letter.
Outputs: The stream is rendered to the terminal with word wrapping and inter-word spaces; returns when the terminator is consumed.
Assumptions: The wrap threshold is a hard-coded 41 ($29) compared against column plus word length. A word longer than forty characters would still overflow. The routine is re-entered recursively in effect through PROCESS_TOKEN, which saves and restores TERM_DATA_PTR on the stack.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, WORD_REMAINING_LEN ($25), TERM_DATA_PTR, WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG, the terminal cursors and CURRENT_COLUMN.
Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through PRINT_CHARACTER.

records.s: scan literal word, measuring its length

records.c:
If CURRENT_COLUMN + WORD_REMAINING_LEN >= $29 (41), emit a newline (PRINT_EMPTY_LINE) before
printing the word (PRINT_WORD). Then TEST_ADD_SPACE adds a separating space unless the next
char is a '.' or we're at column 0.

records.s: If column 0, don't print a space

records.c:
Token id has bit7 set; (id & $7F)*2 indexes TOKEN_POINTERS_BASE_ADDR ($25DD) to get a pointer
to the token's text. Saves the current TERM_DATA_PTR, points it at the token text, PRINT_WORDs
the expansion (capitalised if UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG), then restores TERM_DATA_PTR and resumes
the sentence. Tokens encode frequently-used words to compress the text.

records.s: Can't reach, because `AND 7Fh` clears the high bit.

records.c:
PRINT_WORD ($0ADB)
Purpose: Emit the characters of one literal word or expanded token, applying the inline control codes: '.' prints a full stop and arms capitalisation, '<' emits a line break, $FF takes the following byte as a new text colour, and A-Z are folded to lowercase unless the capitalisation flag is set.
Inputs: TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23) points at the first character; WORD_REMAINING_LEN ($25) is the character count; UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG ($0AFF) selects the case of the next letter.
Outputs: The characters are printed, TERM_DATA_PTR is advanced past them, WORD_REMAINING_LEN reaches zero, and the capitalisation flag is cleared once it has been consumed.
Assumptions: The $FF colour escape consumes one extra byte and decrements the length accordingly, so a stream that ends immediately after $FF would read past the word. Colour values are written straight to CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR without masking.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, TERM_DATA_PTR, WORD_REMAINING_LEN, UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG, CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR ($0286), the terminal cursors and CURRENT_COLUMN.
Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through PRINT_CHARACTER.

records.s: flag set -> keep uppercase, clear flag

records.c: Sets UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG, prints '.', advances the term pointer, and continues the word.

records.s: $FF: read next byte as new colour

records.c:
PRINT_PARAGRAPH_INDENT ($0B3D)
Purpose: Advance to the start of a fresh line and emit a two-space indent, the standard prefix for an inventory item or an event paragraph.
Inputs: None in registers; the terminal cursors and CURRENT_COLUMN ($24) must be valid.
Outputs: The cursor is at column 2 of a new line.
Assumptions: PRINT_EMPTY_LINE reaches column zero by padding with spaces, so this also clears the remainder of the current line.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the terminal cursors, CURRENT_COLUMN, and MEMCPY state if a scroll occurs.
Hardware changes: Writes screen and colour RAM through PRINT_CHARACTER.

PRINT_EMPTY_LINE ($0B4B)
Purpose: Advance the cursor to the start of the next line by printing spaces until the column wraps to zero. If the cursor is already at column zero it still emits a whole blank line.
Inputs: CURRENT_COLUMN ($24) and the terminal cursors.
Outputs: The cursor sits at column zero of a new line; the remainder of the previous line has been overwritten with spaces in the current text colour.
Assumptions: The loop is written as a self tail-jump rather than a counted loop, so it relies on PRINT_CHARACTER resetting the column exactly at 39.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, the terminal cursors, CURRENT_COLUMN, and MEMCPY state if a scroll occurs.
Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM at $CC00-$CFFF and colour RAM at $D800-$DBFF through PRINT_CHARACTER.

PRINT_ROOM_TEXT ($0B58)
Purpose: Print one room description: convert the global room id to a part-relative index, resolve it through the room-text pointer table, emit two leading spaces, draw the first letter as a drop capital, then render the rest of the stream.
Inputs: A = global room id. CURRENT_PART_NO ($2940) selects the base in PART_ROOM_BASE_IDS ($0DCC); the room-text pointer table base is the word at $2F00.
Outputs: The room description printed with its two-by-two initial; TERM_DATA_PTR advanced past the leading letter. Tail-jumps to PROCESS_TERM.
Assumptions: The description's first character is an uppercase A-Z letter, because the drop-cap glyph index is computed as $7B + 4*(char - 'A'). Both the base table and the pointer table live in the replaceable overlay.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, SCRATCH_BYTE ($02), SCRATCH_BYTE_2 ($04), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23), CURRENT_CHAR_COLOR ($0286) which is left at 6, and the terminal state.
Hardware changes: Writes screen and colour RAM through the renderer.

records.s: draw the room description's first letter as a 2x2 drop capital

records.c: Bitmap destination base address for each of the ten illustration character rows.
Screen-RAM destination base address for each of the ten illustration character rows.
Color-RAM destination base address for each of the ten illustration character rows.

ROOM_GRAPHIC_TABLE — 57 fixed six-byte room-illustration descriptors at $0BF9-$0D4E.
RoomGraphicRecord layout, stride 6:
+0 start_row
+1 start_column
+2 source_ptr, little endian
+4 height_rows
+5 width_columns
BLIT_ROOM_GRAPHIC copies these fields into zero-page blit state, then invokes COPY_BLIT_ROW three times per character row. Each source row is interleaved as width*8 bitmap bytes, width screen-matrix bytes, then width colour-RAM bytes. A record therefore consumes height*width*10 bytes. BITMAP_ROW_ADDR_TABLE, SCREEN_ROW_ADDR_TABLE, and COLOR_ROW_ADDR_TABLE select the ten destination rows in bitmap $E000, screen $CC00, and colour RAM $D800.
The captured occupant uses descriptors 0-20. Descriptor 0 points to $A100; descriptors 1-20 form the current contiguous source chain $4300-$93E5 and are fully typed as ROOM_GFX_00 through ROOM_GFX_20. Descriptors 21-56 are resident transition metadata whose addressed payload occupants are absent from this capture; they remain structurally typed descriptors but are not expanded into noncaptured graphics.
The 57-entry extent is established inside the capture: the following byte at $0D4F begins OBJ_ROOM_TABLE, that table's largest descriptor index is $38 (decimal 56), and a hypothetical descriptor at $0D4F has an impossible zero width.

OBJ_ROOM_TABLE ($0D4F-$0DCB) — 125 resident bytes indexed by global room id $00-$7C; each byte selects a RoomGraphicRecord in ROOM_GRAPHIC_TABLE.
At $10A5 the engine indexes this table with CURRENT_ROOM, compares the result with CURRENT_ROOM_GRAPHIC_ID, and repaints when it changes. For the captured current part, rooms $00-$28 select descriptors $00-$14. Bytes for room ids $29-$7C are retained and typed because they are present, but they are transition metadata for noncaptured occupants and are not interpreted as later-part content here. A zero entry means no illustration.

Three-entry table of global-room bases used by captured engine code: $00, $29, $4D. The current captured part uses entry 0. Entries 1 and 2 are resident transition metadata; their replacement occupants are outside this project.

Three little-endian initialization-script pointers indexed by CURRENT_PART_NO. Entry 0 selects the captured part's script at $2968. Entries 1 and 2 address captured bytecode-shaped slots, but a disk transition replaces the overlay containing both scripts and their operand tables; this project does not equate the captured slot bytes with noncaptured occupants.
Pointer to the eight-byte save/load filename buffer.

FILENAME_BUF — eight-byte mutable KERNAL save/load filename buffer, initialized to `FILENAME`. The active code hardcodes its eight-byte capacity; the following word UNUSED_FILENAME_BUFFER_SIZE is redundant metadata and is never read.

UNUSED_FILENAME_BUFFER_SIZE — shipped little-endian constant $0008 immediately after the eight-byte FILENAME_BUF.
READ_FILENAME hardcodes CPY #$08 and SETUP_KERNAL_FILE hardcodes LDA #$08, so neither reads this word. No instruction operand, pointer, table entry, or recorded reference consumes it. It is redundant assembler metadata retained with the disabled save/load subsystem.

ACTION_DISPATCH_TABLE — 33 little-endian action-handler pointers indexed by bytecode opcode. Confirmed targets include ACTION_MOVE_DIRECTION, SCRIPT_SET_OBJECT_LOCATION, ACTION_DROP_OBJECT ($0EB0), ACTION_TAKE_OBJECT ($0F02), counter/flag handlers, inventory, DESCRIBE_CURRENT_ROOM, and other $11xx handlers.

SCRIPT_GOTO_ACTION_SCRIPT_NOUN ($0E25)
Purpose: Action opcode $1E: redirect the running script to the ordinary action stream of the direction the player named. Used by contextual verbs such as FLY and RIDE, which take a direction as their noun.
Inputs: NOUN_ID ($4D) holds the parsed direction token; valid values are $01-$0A.
Outputs: On a valid direction, SCRIPT_PC is replaced with that direction's action stream through RUN_DIRECTION_ACTION_SCRIPT, so the current VM loop resumes there. On zero or a value of $0B or above, sentence $25 is printed and the handler returns.
Assumptions: Direction tokens are one-based and dense; the check is a single unsigned comparison against $0B, so any token below $0B other than zero is treated as a direction.
Clobbers: A, flags, VERB_ID ($4C), SCRIPT_PC ($4E/$4F), and, on the error path, renderer scratch.
Hardware changes: None directly; the error path writes screen and colour RAM through the renderer.
records.s: NOUN_ID is a direction word id for FLY/RIDE <direction>.; Source aliases: SCRIPT_MOVE_NOUN_DIRECTION

records.c:
SCRIPT_GOTO_ACTION_SCRIPT ($0E33)
Purpose: Action opcode $1D: read one literal direction id from the bytecode stream and redirect the running script to that direction's ordinary action stream. Used by ENTER, CLIMB and OUT rules so that a contextual command inherits the real direction's barriers and room transition.
Inputs: One operand byte at SCRIPT_PC; every genuine emission site supplies $01-$0A.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced past the operand, then replaced with the selected direction's action stream; the current VM loop resumes there.
Assumptions: Unlike opcode $1E this path performs no range validation, so a malformed operand would index outside the ten-entry action-script pointer table.
Clobbers: A, flags, VERB_ID ($4C), SCRIPT_PC ($4E/$4F), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D).
Hardware changes: None.
records.s: Fetch one-based direction id ($01-$0A) from action bytecode.; Source aliases: SCRIPT_MOVE_FIXED_DIRECTION

records.c:
RUN_DIRECTION_ACTION_SCRIPT ($0E36)
Purpose: Shared tail of action opcodes $1D and $1E: cache a one-based direction id as the current verb and point SCRIPT_PC at that direction's action script.
Inputs: A = one-based direction id $01-$0A.
Outputs: VERB_ID ($4C) = A; SCRIPT_PC ($4E/$4F) loaded from ACTION_SCRIPT_POINTERS entry A-1. It does not recursively run the VM; the caller's interpreter loop continues at the new address.
Assumptions: The ten direction verbs occupy the first ten action-script slots, so subtracting one converts the verb id to a table index.
Clobbers: A, flags, VERB_ID, SCRIPT_PC, WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D).
Hardware changes: None.

ACTION_MOVE_DIRECTION ($0E3F)
Purpose: The movement handler. Selects one of ten sorted exit tables from the current verb, scans it for an entry whose from-room matches CURRENT_ROOM, and on a match moves the player and describes the destination; otherwise it prints the refusal sentence 2.
Inputs: VERB_ID ($4C) holds a one-based direction id; DIRECTION_EXIT_POINTERS (base word at $16B4) selects the table; CURRENT_ROOM ($293F).
Outputs: On success CURRENT_ROOM is replaced by the destination and control tail-jumps to DESCRIBE_CURRENT_ROOM. On failure it tail-jumps to PRINT_SENTENCE with sentence 2. VERB_ID is decremented and re-incremented, so it is unchanged on exit.
Assumptions: Each exit table is a list of two-byte from/to pairs sorted by from-room and terminated implicitly: the scan stops as soon as an entry's from-room is greater than or equal to CURRENT_ROOM, so the sort order is load bearing.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags, WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), AUX_PTR ($0E/$0F), CURRENT_ROOM on success, and all renderer and graphics scratch through the tail call.
Hardware changes: None directly; the tail calls write screen, colour and bitmap memory.

records.s: Add the low byte of DIRECTION_EXIT_POINTERS.
Match the exit record whose from_room equals CURRENT_ROOM.
Enter the matched exit record's to_room.

records.c:
SCRIPT_SET_CURRENT_ROOM ($0E8D)
Purpose: Action opcode: teleport the player by storing one literal room id into CURRENT_ROOM without running any exit table or description.
Inputs: One operand byte at SCRIPT_PC.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced by one; CURRENT_ROOM ($293F) = operand.
Assumptions: No description or repaint happens here; the script is expected to follow up with a description or graphic opcode.
Clobbers: A, flags, SCRIPT_PC.
Hardware changes: None.

SCRIPT_SET_OBJECT_LOCATION ($0E94)
Purpose: Action opcode: assign an object's location or state. Reads a slot index and a value; the marker $FA is replaced by the current room, which lets one script move an object to wherever the player is.
Inputs: Two operand bytes at SCRIPT_PC: object slot index, then value or the $FA marker.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced by two; OBJECT_LOCATIONS[slot] ($28BF + slot) set to the value, or to CURRENT_ROOM when the value was $FA.
Assumptions: The slot index is not range checked against OBJECT_COUNT ($22A3). Values $FC (carried) and $FD (absent) are reserved states, not room numbers.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags, SCRIPT_PC.
Hardware changes: None.

records.s: Marker $FA means use CURRENT_ROOM as the object location.
Store the selected location/state in OBJECT_LOCATIONS[slot].

records.c:
SET_VERBOSE_OFF ($0EA6)
Purpose: Action opcode: suppress the short confirmation sentences that TAKE and DROP print after a successful action.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: VERBOSE_FLAG ($63) = 0. Returns with A=0 and Z set.
Assumptions: The flag only gates confirmations; refusals and error sentences are printed regardless.
Clobbers: A, flags.
Hardware changes: None.

SET_VERBOSE_ON ($0EAB)
Purpose: Action opcode: re-enable the short confirmation sentences. Also called directly at the end of SETUP_CURRENT_ROOM so that a freshly initialised part starts verbose.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: VERBOSE_FLAG ($63) = 1. Returns with A=1 and Z clear.
Assumptions: Scripts use the off/on pair around a scripted sequence so that its internal object moves stay silent.
Clobbers: A, flags.
Hardware changes: None.

ACTION_DROP_OBJECT ($0EB0)
Purpose: The DROP handler. Requires the command state to permit acting and the resolved noun to be currently carried; moves the object into the current room, decrements the carried count, clears its icon from the visible-record table, and repaints.
Inputs: NOUN_ID ($4D) must be non-zero and must resolve through RESOLVE_NOUN; VERBOSE_FLAG ($63) selects the confirmation.
Outputs: OBJECT_LOCATIONS[slot] set to CURRENT_ROOM; OBJ_COUNTERS[0] decremented; the matching six-byte record in VISIBLE_OBJECT_RECORDS ($2943) zeroed and the picture repainted. Sentence $19 for a blocked state, sentence $0A when the object is not carried, sentence $0D as confirmation.
Assumptions: The record search matches on the object's computed $A560 graphics pointer, so an object whose icon is not currently installed simply falls out of the loop and no repaint occurs.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, CURRENT_OBJECT_INDEX ($5C), GRAPHIC_RECORD_PTR ($5A/$5B), the visible-record table, and all renderer and blitter scratch.
Hardware changes: Writes colour RAM, screen RAM and bitmap memory through RENDER_ROOM_GRAPHICS when a record was cleared.

records.s: Move this carried object into the current room.
Locate the selected object's $A560 graphics block.
Redraw after adding the dropped object's graphic.

records.c:
ACTION_TAKE_OBJECT ($0F02)
Purpose: The TAKE handler. Requires the command state to permit acting, the noun to resolve, the object to be in the current room, and the carry capacity not to be exhausted; marks the object carried, increments the count, installs its icon in the first free visible record, and repaints.
Inputs: NOUN_ID ($4D); RESOLVE_NOUN supplies the slot, the location and the graphics index; OBJ_COUNTERS[0] ($292F) is the carried count and also the capacity gate.
Outputs: OBJECT_LOCATIONS[slot] set to $FC; OBJ_COUNTERS[0] incremented; the icon pointer installed in a free record of VISIBLE_OBJECT_RECORDS and the picture repainted. Refusals use sentence $19 (cannot act), $03 (no noun), $09 (already carried), $08 (not here) and $0B (hands full at count 5).
Assumptions: The capacity test compares OBJ_COUNTERS[0] against the literal 5 before the increment, so the practical limit is five carried objects. If every visible record is occupied the icon is silently not installed and no repaint occurs.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, CURRENT_OBJECT_INDEX ($5C), GRAPHIC_RECORD_PTR ($5A/$5B), the visible-record table, and all renderer and blitter scratch.
Hardware changes: Writes colour RAM, screen RAM and bitmap memory through RENDER_ROOM_GRAPHICS.

records.s: Is this object located in CURRENT_ROOM?
Mark the selected object as carried.
Find an unused visible-object graphic record.
Locate the selected object's $A560 graphics block.
Install the object graphic pointer in the free record.
Redraw after removing the taken object's room graphic.

records.c:
CALC_OBJECT_GRAPHIC_PTR ($0F70)
Purpose: Compute the address of an object icon: GRAPHIC_RECORD_PTR = $A560 + CURRENT_OBJECT_INDEX * $A0, using repeated sixteen-bit addition rather than a multiply.
Inputs: CURRENT_OBJECT_INDEX ($5C) = icon slot index.
Outputs: GRAPHIC_RECORD_PTR ($5A/$5B) points at the selected 160-byte icon record. Index 0 returns the base unchanged.
Assumptions: The $A0 stride is the fixed icon record size; the table holds 36 slots from $A560 to $BBDF. The routine does not bound the index.
Clobbers: A, Y, flags, GRAPHIC_RECORD_PTR. X is preserved.
Hardware changes: None.
records.s: Start at the object graphics base $A560.
Scale CURRENT_OBJECT_INDEX by $A0 to select its graphics block.
Object graphic index 0 already selects the base block.
Advance one $A0-byte block per object graphic index.

records.c:
STATE_SET_COUNTER ($0F8B)
Purpose: Action opcode: assign a counter. Reads an index and a value from the bytecode and stores the value into OBJ_COUNTERS[index].
Inputs: Two operand bytes at SCRIPT_PC: index, then value.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced by two; OBJ_COUNTERS[index] ($292F + index) = value.
Assumptions: Counters share the 48-byte state block with flags; the index is not range checked.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, SCRATCH_INDEX ($03), SCRIPT_PC.
Hardware changes: None.

STATE_INC_COUNTER ($0F99)
Purpose: Action opcode: increment a counter, saturating at $FF so a long-running tally cannot wrap to zero.
Inputs: One operand byte at SCRIPT_PC: the counter index.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced by one; OBJ_COUNTERS[index] incremented unless it was already $FF.
Assumptions: Saturation is explicit, which matters because several scripts test counters for exact values.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, SCRIPT_PC.
Hardware changes: None.

STATE_DEC_COUNTER ($0FA8)
Purpose: Action opcode: decrement a counter, flooring at zero so it cannot wrap to $FF.
Inputs: One operand byte at SCRIPT_PC: the counter index.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced by one; OBJ_COUNTERS[index] decremented unless it was already zero.
Assumptions: The floor is explicit and is the mirror of the saturating increment.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, SCRIPT_PC.
Hardware changes: None.

STATE_SET_FLAG ($0FB5)
Purpose: Action opcode: set a Boolean progression flag to one.
Inputs: One operand byte at SCRIPT_PC: the flag index.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced by one; OBJ_FLAGS[index] ($290F + index) = 1.
Assumptions: Flags occupy $290F-$293E; index 7 is the room-lit flag consulted by DESCRIBE_CURRENT_ROOM. The index is not range checked.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, SCRIPT_PC.
Hardware changes: None.

STATE_CLEAR_FLAG ($0FBF)
Purpose: Action opcode: clear a Boolean progression flag to zero.
Inputs: One operand byte at SCRIPT_PC: the flag index.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced by one; OBJ_FLAGS[index] = 0.
Assumptions: Clearing index 7 makes the room dark, which suppresses the whole room description.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, SCRIPT_PC.
Hardware changes: None.

RETURN_SKIP_CALLER ($0FC9)
Purpose: Action opcode: a one-level non-local exit. Discards the immediate caller's return address so the following RTS lands in the caller's caller, unwinding out of the interpreter loop that invoked the handler.
Inputs: The stack must hold this handler's return address on top of the return address to be skipped.
Outputs: Two bytes popped, then RTS. A holds the last byte popped and N/Z reflect it; X, Y and the other flags are preserved.
Assumptions: The handler is invoked through the self-modified JSR at $1699, so the address discarded is always RUN_SCRIPT's, and control resumes in whatever called RUN_SCRIPT.
Clobbers: A, N and Z, and two bytes of stack depth.
Hardware changes: None.

ACTION_QUIT ($0FCC)
Purpose: The QUIT handler: print the confirmation prompt, read one key, and either fall into the non-returning restart or return quietly.
Inputs: None in registers; the terminal and keyboard must be usable.
Outputs: Sentence $34 printed. On uppercase 'Y' control falls into RESTART_GAME and does not return; on any other key a blank line is printed and the handler returns normally.
Assumptions: CHECK_YES_KEY only accepts uppercase 'Y', and the fall-through into RESTART_GAME is deliberate, which is why the confirmation branch has no JMP.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, keyboard workspace and renderer scratch.
Hardware changes: Reads the CIA 1 keyboard matrix through KERNAL SCNKEY and GETIN; writes screen and colour RAM.

RESTART_GAME ($0FDD)
Purpose: Abandon the current command entirely and restart the adventure. Pops three nested return addresses to unwind the handler, interpreter and dispatcher frames, prints the restart message, and jumps to the initialisation entry.
Inputs: Entered through the normal three-level command call stack: DISPATCH_COMMAND calls RUN_SCRIPT, which calls the handler through the self-modified JSR.
Outputs: Six bytes popped from the stack; sentence $35 printed; control transferred to CALL_INIT_GAME. Non-returning.
Assumptions: The exact stack depth is part of the contract; a caller that reached this code by any other route would return into rubbish. The stack pointer is not otherwise repaired, so the abandoned frames' contents are simply left behind.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, six bytes of stack, and all game state through the reinitialisation.
Hardware changes: None directly; the reinitialisation path writes screen, colour and bitmap memory.

ACTION_NEXT_PART ($0FF1)
Purpose: The story-advance handler: unwind the command dispatch, clear the progression flag that gates the transition, and jump into the multipart loader path.
Inputs: Entered through the same three-level command call stack as RESTART_GAME; the replacement disk part must be available.
Outputs: Six bytes popped; OBJ_FLAGS[2] ($2911) cleared; control transferred to SWITCH_TO_NEXT_PART. Non-returning.
Assumptions: As with RESTART_GAME the three-frame depth is load bearing. After the transition the captured overlay, its tables and its scripts are replaced, so nothing beyond the loader contract can be asserted about the successor occupant.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, six bytes of stack, and, through the callees, the overlay, display, IRQ, CIA and banking state.
Hardware changes: Through SHOW_PART_LOAD_SCREEN and LOAD_NEXT_GAME_PART: VIC-II display enable and border, $D01A, $D019, CIA 1 $DC0D/$DC0E, CIA 2 $DD0D, the serial bus, and the 6510 port $01.

ACTION_PRINT_MESSAGE ($1001)
Purpose: Action opcode: fetch one event-text id from the bytecode stream and render that event paragraph.
Inputs: One operand byte at SCRIPT_PC: the event-text id.
Outputs: SCRIPT_PC advanced by one; the event paragraph printed with a blank line and two-space indent.
Assumptions: The event pointer table lives in the replaceable overlay at $2F02, so the same id selects different prose after a part change.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, SCRIPT_PC, TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG and terminal state.
Hardware changes: Writes screen and colour RAM through the renderer.

CMD_INVENTORY ($1008)
Purpose: The INVENTORY handler: print the header sentence, then walk the object table and print the description of every object whose location byte is the carried marker $FC. If nothing is carried it prints the 'nothing' sentence instead.
Inputs: OBJECT_LOCATIONS ($28BF) and OBJECT_COUNT ($22A3); the object-description pointer table base is the word at $1C6B.
Outputs: Sentence $0E, then one indented paragraph per carried object, or sentence $0F when none; finally a blank line.
Assumptions: The scan bound is OBJECT_COUNT, a captured overlay byte, so the list length follows the current part. Each description pointer addresses a length-prefixed token stream and the routine skips that length byte before rendering.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, LOOP_COUNTER ($4B), WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), AUX_PTR ($0E/$0F), TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23), UPPERCASE_LETTER_FLAG, and terminal state; the loop index is preserved across each item on the stack.
Hardware changes: Writes screen and colour RAM through the renderer.

DESCRIBE_CURRENT_ROOM ($107E)
Purpose: Enter a room for presentation purposes: refuse everything if the room-lit flag is clear, otherwise print the room text, list the objects lying here, and synchronise the illustration with the room's default picture, repainting only if it changed.
Inputs: OBJ_FLAGS[7] ($2916) is the room-lit flag; CURRENT_ROOM ($293F); OBJ_ROOM_TABLE ($0D4F) maps room id to default picture id; CURRENT_ROOM_GRAPHIC_ID ($2942).
Outputs: Either sentence $3F alone when dark, or the room description, the list of present objects, and a possibly updated CURRENT_ROOM_GRAPHIC_ID with a repaint.
Assumptions: Darkness is checked before anything else, so a dark room hides both prose and object list but leaves the previous illustration on screen. The picture is only redrawn when the default id actually changes, which is what makes scripted overrides persist.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, WORK_PTR ($0C/$0D), AUX_PTR ($0E/$0F), TERM_DATA_PTR ($22/$23), the self-modified operand at $1109, renderer and blitter scratch.
Hardware changes: Writes screen RAM, colour RAM and bitmap memory through the renderer and RENDER_ROOM_GRAPHICS.

records.s: List it when its location equals CURRENT_ROOM.

records.c:
NOOP_ACTION_11 ($1125)
Purpose: Action opcode $0B: a deliberate no-op verb body. Calls the RTS stub NOOP_0699 and returns, so the enclosing script's next opcode supplies the canned reply.
Inputs: None.
Outputs: No semantic state change. Returns to the interpreter.
